title: Conformable Wearable Electrodes: From Fabrication to Electrophysiological Assessment
protocol: Cut a piece of the substrate of interest.
Wash tattoo substrate with water before printing to remove the topmost, water-soluble layer from the paper.
Use glue sheet provided in the tattoo paper kit both to enhance tattoo adhesion and as a passivation layer.
Cut the substrate of interest for wearable sensors.
Place the cut substrate on the printer plate and tape its border to keep it flat.
Prepare the design to print, such as a circle (12 mm diameter) with a rectangular pad at the bottom (3 mm x 7 mm).
Filter the PEDOT:PSS commercial ink through a filter before filling the printer cartridges (10 pl).
Print the designed pattern on the substrate using a drop spacing of ~20 µm for tattoo paper and textile.
Print multiple layers of PEDOT:PSS either consecutively or with drying at 110 °C for 15 min between layers to create a homogeneous and continuous conductive pattern.
Dry the printed electrode at 110 °C for 15 min in an oven to complete solvent evaporation.
Cut a rectangular piece of polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) substrate (8 mm x 12 mm, 1.3 mm thickness).
Print a rectangular design (3 mm x 12 mm) with three PEDOT:PSS layers on top of the substrate.
Dry the printed sample in the oven at 110 °C for 15 min.
Laminate the PEN interconnection onto the tattoo electrode, with the PEDOT:PSS rectangular parts facing each other.
Cut a hole (diameter 11.3 mm) in the tattoo paper glue sheet.
Align this hole of the glue sheet with the circular sensing part of the tattoo PEDOT:PSS electrode.
Add a piece of polyimide tape onto the free end of the PEN interconnection.
Attach a piece of conductive tape around the rectangular printed connection to obtain a robust and stable interconnection.
Plug a pogo pin connector into the copper tape and connect the pogo pin to the recording system.
Remove the glue liner.
Place the tattoo onto the desired portion of the skin.
Wet the back support paper, keeping the tattoo in position.
Once the back support paper is soaked, slide it to remove it, leaving only the electrode made of the transferable ultrathin film on the skin.
Plug the flat PEN contact into the external acquisition unit.
Place the electrode on the skin.
Secure the electrode with a fabric sports bracelet or medical tape for stable contact during movement.
Perform surface electrophysiological recording.
Wash tattoo electrodes away by rubbing them with a wet sponge after recordings.
Ensure the volunteer is comfortably seated with an arm resting on a table.
Place one electrode and connect it to the working electrode-sensing electrode (WE-S) of the EIS.
Place another electrode 3 cm apart from the first one and connect it to the counter electrode (CE) of the EIS.
Place the third electrode on the elbow and connect it to the reference electrode (RE) of the EIS.
Start recording on the EIS potentiostat.
Apply current between the counter and working electrodes.
Measure potential variation across the reference and sensing couple.
Place ECG electrodes on the left and right clavicles for classical location, or in multiple body areas such as chest, wrists, and ribs, maintaining a minimum interelectrode distance of 6 cm.
Place ground electrode for ECG on the left iliac crest when using classical location.
Position EMG electrodes along the muscle of interest such as biceps or calf.
Attach ground electrode for EMG on a static location like an adjacent bone.
Distribute EEG electrodes in multiple locations on the head.
